q: 1. A square column carries a load P at the centroid of one of the quarters of the square, the side of the main square, the combined bending stress will be
explain: Applying combined direct and bending stress formulas for a load placed at the centroid of one quadrant (eccentricity a/4 in both directions) of a square column of side a gives a combined stress of 3P/a².

q: 2. The Young's modulus of elasticity of steel is
explain: The standard value for steel modulus ($E$) is $200 	ext{ GPa}$ or $200 	ext{ kN/mm}^2$.

q: 3. Creep of material is the property indicated by
options: elongation of the materials caused by changes in material properties
time dependent strain of the materials
shortening caused by shrinkage of the member
decrease in volume of the materials affected by the weather conditions
explain: Creep is specifically defined as permanent deformation under a constant load over time.

q: 4. The shear center may be defined as
options: the point through which the resultant of the shear stress pass
the point about which the moment of shear flow is zero
the centre of gravity of section
explain: The shear center is the point where a load produces only bending and no torsion.

q: 5. The shear center in the case of T-beam section is
options: at the C.G. of the section
at the neutral axis of the section
on the C.G. horizontal plane and away from C.G. within the leg projections
explain: For sections with one axis of symmetry, the shear center lies on that axis. In a T-beam, it is typically at the junction of the web and flange.

q: 6. The shear flow in a section can be defined as
options: total shear stress at a point
explain: Shear flow ($q$) is the shear force per unit length along a cross-section ($q = 	au \cdot t$).

q: 7. When a thin cylindrical shell is subjected to internal fluid pressure, which of the following stress is developed in its wall ?
explain: Internal pressure in cylinders creates both hoop (circumferential) and longitudinal stresses.

q: 8. Euler's formulae for columns can be used if the slenderness ratio is
explain: Euler's formula is valid for long columns with high slenderness ratio, generally taken as greater than about 120, where buckling (not crushing) governs failure.

q: 9. Shear strain theory for the failure of a material at elastic limit is due to
explain: The shear strain energy (distortion energy) theory of failure is attributed to Von Mises (also known as the Von Mises-Hencky theory).

q: 10. Gradually applied static loads do not change with time their
explain: A static load, by definition, is applied gradually and remains constant in magnitude, direction, and point of application over time — hence 'all of these'.

q: 11. The sum of normal stress is
explain: The sum of normal stresses on two mutually perpendicular planes at a point (σx + σy) is a stress invariant — it remains constant regardless of the orientation of the planes chosen.

q: 12. The radius of Mohr's circle for two equal unlike principle stresses of magnitude P is
explain: For two equal but unlike (opposite sign) principal stresses +P and −P, the radius of Mohr's circle = (σ1−σ2)/2 = (P−(−P))/2 = P.

q: 13. Shear stress on principal planes is
explain: By definition, principal planes are those on which shear stress is zero (only normal stress acts).

q: 14. Coefficient of wind resistance of a circular surface is
explain: The standard coefficient of wind resistance (pressure coefficient) for a circular (cylindrical) surface, as used in practical wind load calculations, is taken as 2/3.

q: 15. The ratio of circumferential stress to the longitudinal stress in the walls of a cylindrical shell due to flowing liquid is
explain: For a thin cylindrical shell under internal pressure, circumferential (hoop) stress = pd/2t while longitudinal stress = pd/4t, giving a ratio of 2:1.

q: 16. In a tensile test, when the material is stressed beyond beyond elastic limit, the tensile strain ............. as compared to the stress.
explain: Beyond the elastic limit, the stress-strain curve flattens considerably, meaning strain increases much more rapidly than the corresponding increase in stress.

q: 17. In compression test, the fracture in cast in cast iron specimen would occur along
options: at right angles to the axis of specimen
explain: Cast iron, being weak in shear, typically fails in compression tests along an oblique (diagonal) plane where shear stress is maximum, rather than perpendicular to the load axis.

q: 18. The ratio of lateral strain to axial strain of a homogenous material is known as
explain: By definition, Poisson's ratio is the ratio of lateral strain to axial (longitudinal) strain.

q: 19. The normal and tangential components of stress on an inclined plane through to the direction of the force will be equal to
explain: For a uniaxial stress acting on an inclined plane, the normal and tangential (shear) stress components become equal when the plane is inclined at 45° to the force direction.

q: 20. The locus of the end point of the resultant of the normal and tangential components of the stress on an inclined plane is
explain: As the inclination of the plane varies, the resultant stress vector's endpoint traces out an ellipse (the stress ellipse), similar to the momental ellipse for inertia.

q: 21. Principal planes are subjected to
options: normal stresses as well as tangential stresses
explain: By definition, a principal plane carries only normal stress with zero shear (tangential) stress.

q: 22. A bar l meter long and having its area of cross section A, is subjected to a gradually applied load W. the strain energy stored in the bar is
explain: Strain energy stored in a bar under a gradually applied axial load W is U = W²L/2AE, the standard formula (area under the linear load-deformation curve).

q: 23. Glass will obey Hooke's law up to
explain: Being a brittle material with no distinct yield point, glass behaves elastically (obeying Hooke's law) right up until sudden fracture.

q: 24. The proportional limit of mild steel specimen is taken as the stress, corresponding to permanent set of
explain: The proportional limit for mild steel is conventionally defined based on a very small permanent set of 0.01%, essentially marking the true elastic/proportional behavior limit.

q: 25. If a material has identical properties in all directions, it is said to be
explain: Isotropic means having identical mechanical properties in every direction at a point, as opposed to homogeneous (uniform properties throughout the material, but possibly directionally dependent).

q: 26. When a member is subjected to axial tensile load, the greatest normal stress is equal to
explain: Under uniaxial tension σ, the maximum shear stress is σ/2, so the greatest normal stress (σ) is twice the maximum shear stress.

q: 27. Hooke's law states that stress and strain are
explain: Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 28. A shaft is subjected to bending moment M and a torque T simultaneously. The ratio of the maximum bending stress to maximum shear stress developed in the shaft is
explain: Comparing bending stress (σ = 32M/πd³) to shear stress (τ = 16T/πd³) for a circular shaft gives a ratio σ/τ = 2M/T.

q: 29. The greatest load which a spring can carry without getting permanently distorted is called
explain: Proof load is defined as the maximum load a spring can withstand without undergoing permanent deformation.

q: 30. Limit of proportionality depends upon
explain: The limit of proportionality (where Hooke's law ceases to apply) is an intrinsic material property, depending on the type of material rather than its geometry or loading type.

q: 31. If the Young's modulus of elasticity of a material is twice of its modulus of rigidity, the Poisson's ratio of the material is
explain: Using E = 2G(1+μ), if E = 2G, then 2G = 2G(1+μ), giving 1+μ=1, so μ = 0 (zero).

q: 32. For an isotropic, homogenous and elastic material obeying Hooke's law, number of independent elastic constant is
explain: For an isotropic homogeneous elastic material, only 2 independent elastic constants (e.g., E and G, or E and Poisson's ratio) are needed, since all others can be derived from these.

q: 33. A close coil helical spring when subjected to a moment M having its axis along the axis of helix is
options: it is subjected to pure bending
its number of coil will increase
explain: When a closed-coil spring is subjected to a moment about its own (helix) axis, the wire experiences pure bending (as opposed to axial loading which causes torsion).

q: 34. The stress below which a material has a high probability of not failing under reversal of stress is known as
explain: The endurance limit (fatigue limit) is defined as the maximum stress below which a material can withstand an infinite number of stress reversals (cycles) without fatigue failure.

q: 35. In a rectangular shaft subjected to torsion, the maximum shear stress occurs at
explain: For a rectangular (non-circular) shaft under torsion, the maximum shear stress occurs at the midpoint of the longer side, per membrane analogy/torsion theory for non-circular sections.

q: 36. Impact test enables to estimate the property of
explain: Impact tests (like Charpy/Izod) measure the energy absorbed during fracture, which is a direct measure of a material's toughness.

q: 37. The phenomenon of decreased resistance of a material to reversal of stress is called
explain: Fatigue is defined as the progressive reduction in a material's strength/resistance under repeated or reversed cyclic stress, even below its static strength.

q: 38. The property of metal which allows it to deform continuously at slow rate without any further increase in stress is known as
explain: Creep is the property allowing continuous, slow deformation of a material under sustained constant stress over time.

q: 39. Within the elastic range of a tensile test the deviation from Hooke's law and some after effect may be noticed. This is due to
options: material does not at all obey hooke's law
elastic limit is greater than ultimate strength
explain: Minor deviations and after-effects within the nominally elastic range are typically attributed to thermo-elastic effects (temperature changes accompanying rapid elastic deformation).

q: 40. In a shaft, the shear stress is not directly proportional to
explain: From τ = Gθr/L, shear stress is proportional to radius, angle of twist, and modulus of rigidity, but is inversely (not directly) proportional to the length of the shaft.

q: 41. Which of the following is a proper sequence?
options: Proportional limit, elastic limit, yielding, failure
Elastic limit, proportional limit, elastic limit, failure
Yielding, proportional limit, elastic limit, failure
explain: On a typical stress-strain curve for a ductile material, the sequence of milestones as stress increases is: proportional limit, then elastic limit, then yielding, then eventual failure.

q: 42. The torsional rigidity of a shafts given by
explain: Torsional rigidity is defined as the torque required to produce a unit angle of twist, given by T/φ (equivalently GJ).

q: 43. The limit of eccentricity for no tensile conditions for a column of circular section of diameter (d) is
explain: The eccentricity limit (core radius) for a circular column of diameter d is d/8 (i.e., radius r/4 = d/8), beyond which tension develops.
